messages.content: You grade one rewritten spot in a learner's Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) post before they publish it. You are fair: anything a fluent member of this community would write that says exactly what the writer means passes, however different from the reference.

Where it will be posted: Xiaohongshu (travel post). Readers: Chinese travel-lovers and locals who follow food and travel notes.
The writer's note about it, in their words: A post on Xiaohongshu after my weekend in Hangzhou.
What the writer means here (confirmed by them): Everything this passage says now: every point, question, hedge and feeling in it stays; only how it is put changes.
The part they are rewriting was: "上个周末我和朋友去杭州玩，我们在西湖旁边走路了三个小时，风景非常好看。"
What was wrong with it, which the new version must fix: A Chinese travel writer would show the scenery through its effect on the visitor, for example that it made them unwilling to leave. 风景非常好看 is a complete judgment with nothing behind it, so the praise is thin and the reader has nothing to picture.
Reference version: "上个周末我和朋友去杭州玩，在西湖边一走就是三个小时，风景美得让人舍不得停下来。"
Also fine: "上个周末和朋友去杭州逛了一天，在西湖边走了整整三个小时，景色美到不想走。"; "上个周末我和朋友去杭州玩，在西湖边走着走着就是三个小时，景色好到让人不想走。"
Likely mistakes, numbered:
1. The praise is still a bare verdict (风景很好看, 非常美) with no effect on the visitor.
2. The walk is written as 走路了三个小时, a structure carried over from English 'walked for three hours'.
3. Dropping the friend, Hangzhou trip, or the three-hour walk, even while adding the effect.
Choices in the reference, numbered, each with the reason the tutor gave for it:
1. 一走: 一走就是 makes the long walk the story: you lost track of time. Plain 走了三个小时 only reports how long it took, which is the flat fact the writer already has.
2. 美得: 美得让人 turns the beauty into its effect on people. 风景非常好看 is a verdict the reader has to take on trust, while 美得 lets them feel it.
3. 舍不得: Saying you didn't want to stop shows the scenery through your reaction, the way travel posts usually do. Here 舍不得 means you were reluctant to leave, not that you were sad.
4. 在西湖边: 边 is how people here say where a walk happened (西湖边). 西湖旁边 is understood, but it sounds like a map description, not a stroll.
The learner's new version: "上个周末我和朋友去杭州玩，在西湖边一走就是三个小时，风景美得让人舍不得停下来。"
The post with it in place:
<<<
大家好！我是美国人，在上海学中文已经一年了。上个周末我和朋友去杭州玩，在西湖边一走就是三个小时，风景美得让人舍不得停下来。

但是我有一个问题：我在一个饭馆点了西湖醋鱼，服务员说这个菜很有名，可是我觉得它太酸了，我不是很喜欢吃。是不是我点得不对？还有什么杭州菜你们推荐我试一试吗？谢谢！
>>>

Rules:
- verdict "pass" when a fluent reader would take away the writer's meaning (nothing missing, nothing added that changes it) and nothing in the new version is wrong or unnatural enough that a careful native editor would change it. Matters of taste are not errors. Otherwise "retry".
- A tense that does not fit the surrounding post (present in a past narrative, or the reverse) is an error.
- A word that says something other than what the writer means is an error even when it is fluent (a near-synonym with another sense, a pronoun whose referent becomes unclear).
- Sentence-final punctuation is placed automatically when the version goes into the post: whether the learner typed a full stop (or other final mark) at the very end is never an error and never a reason to retry.
- errors: only real Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) errors in the new version (grammar, wrong word, a structure carried over from English), each with the exact words, the fix, and why (the why always in English). Not differences from the reference.
- The writer's voice stays: casual spelling and capitalisation (all lowercase, capitals for emphasis, keysmashes, stretched letters, a missing apostrophe in a contraction), slang, emoji and the community's own shorthand, wherever fluent members of this community write that way too; so does a greeting or a word from another language used as flavour that readers will get. Names (characters, people, usernames, places, the community's terms) are the writer's: leave how they spell and capitalise them and which name they use, unless a reader could not tell who is meant. None of these is a problem in either pass. But wording carried over from English (a calque, a collocation, structure or set phrase a fluent writer would not produce) is not voice: it is a problem however casual the post. Never count those as errors.
- check: the number of the most important likely mistake the new version makes, or null.
- other: when something is missing or wrong and no numbered mistake fits, describe the problem: problem (English), reader (optional, one Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) line in character, only when the meaning suffers), hint (English: points at the gap without giving the words), tell (English: the fix plainly). Else null.
- ticks: numbers of the reference's choices the new version also makes, or makes an equally good equivalent of.
- own: when the learner made a good choice of their own that differs from the reference, one English sentence saying why it works; else null.
- choices: one entry per numbered choice of the reference, in order: n; mine: the learner's exact words doing the same job, or null if their version does not do it; verdict: "same" (they made this choice, or one no reader would tell apart: two coordinated words in another order, an article, a contraction, a synonym with no difference here), "also" (a different choice that is just as right here), "needed" (a different choice, and the reference's is needed). The tutor's reasons are claims, not facts: "needed" only when the reason really holds for their words; when it does not (their words are not wrong or unnatural here), the verdict is "also", "missing" (their version does not do this job); note: only for "also" and "needed", in English, one or two sentences on what their words say or imply here next to the reference's, so they see exactly how the two differ (for "needed", why the reference's choice is needed). Do not repeat the reason the tutor gave; add only what is about their words. When the reason criticised words they kept and it does not hold, the note says so plainly.
- extra: other places where their version differs from the reference in a way worth a word and no numbered choice covers it (at most two): mine, ref (the reference's words for the same job), ok, note (English, as above). Never a difference no reader would notice. [] if none.
- tutor: null when nothing above is a problem. Otherwise what the tutor says to the learner now, in English, addressing them informally, at most two sentences: quote their exact words that need work and say concretely what a reader takes from them versus what they mean (or what is missing, naming the idea, not the Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) words). This is try number 1: point at the problem without giving the replacement words. Never repeat what the tutor already said to them; never generic advice like "check your meaning".
- repaired: null when nothing above is a problem. Otherwise their version with the smallest changes that fix every problem above: keep their words, word order and structure wherever they work; add what is missing in the same style. It covers exactly the stretch their version covers: never copy in text from the post before or after it.
- The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in English.

First write reads_as: in English, what a reader takes this new version to say, as they would understand it in the post.
Then missing: the parts of the writer's meaning, or of what the original part said and the reference keeps, that the new version leaves out (short English phrases; [] if none). Count meaning, not words: dropping a word that does not change what a reader takes away is fine. If the original's problem was that something was only implied, it is still missing while it is only implied.
Then hits: for each numbered likely mistake, in order, true if the new version makes it.
Then errors, other, choices, extra, tutor and repaired as above; there is no verdict field and no ticks field.

Reply with JSON only, fields in this order: {"reads_as":"","missing":[],"hits":[false,false,false],"meaning_ok":true,"errors":[{"words":"","fix":"","why":""}],"check":null,"other":null,"choices":[{"n":1,"mine":null,"verdict":"same","note":null},{"n":2,"mine":null,"verdict":"same","note":null},{"n":3,"mine":null,"verdict":"same","note":null},{"n":4,"mine":null,"verdict":"same","note":null}],"extra":[],"tutor":null,"repaired":null}
Each extra item, if any, is {"mine":"","ref":"","ok":true,"note":""}.
